High Definition Vinyl Will Soon Become a Market Reality

There's several sides to this IMHO, and I can't be certain the result.

Vinyl sounds amazing on a good system, especially high quality produced albums from the 70's honestly. If you are a music lover and haven't watched Muscle Shoals http://www.imdb.com/title/tt2492916/ I highly recommend it. The effort to create a master of that quality is immense, but it only truly shines in vinyl. I haven't heard a digital version of music from that era that is close to the analog sound of a real album. Having a sound that good will boost sales if this product is what it claims. If you had the choice of listening to a digitally clipped version of Stairway to Heaven, or a near-perfect analog rendition which would you pick?

Another side is people wanting physical media to enjoy, and relish in the soundscape created by not only artists of an instrument, but artists of the world of sound. This fact gives prominence to the producer, and engineer of the sound. A musician or band can write a great song, but if it isn't recorded and engineered to a super-high quality it will sound poor. This promotes engineers, producers, and bands all the same. It can raise the level of talent, and focus on the recording technique.

Lastly it gives giant corporations and labels a profit model. They can buy up the rights to this process, own the facility, and demand the lion's share of the profits. It also gives another source of revenue to them. This promotes bad things, and a loss to real musicians. A studio capable of recording superior quality music will charge a premium for this service, and a musician or band looking to record will only afford it with the backing of major label.

One up-side is now that 3D printing is moving forward at a lightening pace this capability will move down the veritable food chain. I wouldn't be surprised that in 10 years printing an HD album at home will be as cheap as burning a CD is now.
Vinyl is nice but it does not have the warmth of wax cylinders.
